title: Every translation passes layered checks before it publishes, and correctors fix it after
description:
As an editor, I want each localization checked against the exact original version before it is published automatically, and held when it changes facts, so JIT translations never publish a changed number or claim.

Ryan's decision 2: a translation is not blocked on a human reviewer. Layers before publish: rule checks (numbers, dates, units, URLs, citation keys, quotation count and markers, Markus structure, glossary and do-not-translate names; language-aware, since fact_check.py is English-only), a bilingual model judge block by block, Humanus with target-language policies. High-severity findings get one repair pass; if they persist the localization is held and subscribers are told it needs a person. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450), revised 2026-11-12 with Ryan's decisions.

Feature: Checking translations before JIT publish

Scenario: A changed figure holds the translation
  Given an English paragraph says 40 percent
  When its Spanish translation says 14 por ciento and the repair pass does not fix it
  Then the Spanish localization is not published
  And Spanish subscribers are told it needs a person, with a link to the block

Scenario: Softened certainty is repaired
  Given an English sentence says a policy may change
  When the first translation says it will change
  Then the judge reports changed certainty and the repair pass translates that block again

Scenario: No subscribed reviewer does not block publishing
  Given nobody is subscribed to Chinese translation notifications
  When a Chinese localization passes its checks
  Then it is published and labelled as translated by AI
